verdict.rationale: Kong documents an MCP Traffic Gateway that governs, secures and observes MCP traffic, and catalogs MCP servers. Existing MCP servers can therefore sit behind Kong and have their tools brokered to clients. There is no evidence that Kong itself acts as an MCP client that consumes and invokes those tools. Missing for 10: documented first-party MCP-client capability where the product calls tools from plugged-in servers, step-by-step docs for registering external MCP servers, and hands-on corroboration.
